title: My dad called to say he was stuck in traffic and running late for dinner. He was already sitting at the table.
story:
It was just after seven when my phone buzzed. Dad. He said the highway was backed up and we should start eating without him.

I looked across the table. Dad was right there, passing my mom the potatoes.

I laughed and told the phone it was a good prank. The voice on the line went quiet. Then it said, very calmly, "Who is sitting in my chair?"

I hung up. Mom hadn't heard any of it. The man at the table smiled at me and asked how school was going. I graduated four years ago.

I watched him through the rest of dinner. He held his fork wrong. He laughed a beat after everyone else. And when the dog walked past, he lifted his feet off the floor, slowly, like the dog was something he had been warned about.

At eight the phone buzzed again. A text this time.

"I'm in the driveway. Don't open the door until I knock twice. If you hear one knock, it isn't me."

I read it under the table, my hands shaking.

That was when I noticed the chair across from me was empty.

Then, from the front door, one knock.
premise: dad calls to say he's late while a dad-copy sits at dinner; copy leaves the table and knocks once
theme: family member who isn't quite right
